remaining_concerns: The admissible record still shows a current telehealth discharge planning regression below the warning threshold for a named launch use case.
The policy predicate still requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is still no admissible evidence that the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and explicitly discloses the telehealth limitation.
There is still no admissible evidence of approved mitigation or approved risk acceptance covering the current subgroup weakness.
The certification position remains conditional on a documentation or mitigation predicate that is described as necessary but is not evidenced as satisfied in the current record.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the key missing predicates. The clarified argument is narrower and more accurate than an unconditional approval claim, but it is still a reinterpretation of the same record rather than proof that the current-release policy condition has been met. That distinction matters here: a caveated position can support compliant_with_caveats only when the caveat is a bounded disclosure condition already evidenced as satisfied or otherwise permissible under policy. In this record, the caveat is itself the unresolved compliance predicate: policy allows certification only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence supports aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, but it also shows a current telehealth regression and no evidence of the required current disclosure or approved mitigation. Prior approval and informal monitoring remain contextual only. Because the initial concerns were not closed by genuinely new admissible evidence, the claim remains plausible but insufficiently supported, so the final verdict stays suspicious.
